answer: A credible anti-Sybil check could rest on slow relic stewardship in shale country. Each applicant adopts one shale outcrop and a relic beside it, such as a rusted tool, then visits through four seasons, photographing erosion and the relic's changing patina. From each layer they grind a tiny pigment sample, whose hue depends on that stratum's minerals, so a forged portfolio would need matching pigments from many distant outcrops. Neighbors cross-check samples and visit logs, making dozens of fake identities cost years of fieldwork while one honest keeper tends ground they already walk.
